## Detailed Findings

#### 1. YOLO mode removal + auto-approve migration (core, ~3h, SKIP)

- **What**: Cline #13126 remove YOLO mode setting, migrate old users to auto-approve all. The SDK extension's YOLO toggle was cosmetic: nothing in the approval path read it, so runs were silently governed by the per-action auto-approval settings underneath (cline/cline#13114). Instead of keeping a parallel override system, remove the setting entirely and make the auto-approve menu the single source of truth. Drop yoloModeToggled (and autoApproveAllToggled) from state keys, settings handlers, state posts, telemetry, remote-config yoloModeAllowed transform, settings protos (field numbers reserved). Remove Yolo Mode toggle from Settings -> Features (whole Experimental section, only entry) and "Auto-approve: YOLO" AutoApproveBar takeover. Add v3 storage migration folding previously-enabled YOLO / auto-approve-all toggle into autoApprovalSettings by enabling every action, so previously-unattended setups keep running unattended.
- **Why**: Alexi CLI has no YOLO mode (grep 'yolo|YOLO' in src/ returns zero matches). Alexi uses permission system via src/permission/ (src/permission/index.ts, src/permission/manager.ts). Would be LOW priority if Alexi had YOLO mode (simplifies approval UX, removes cosmetic toggle). Skip for now (no YOLO mode, permission system already single source of truth).
- **Source**: Cline PR #13126 "feat(vscode): remove YOLO mode setting, migrate old users to auto-approve all" (merged 2026-08-10, commit sha unknown). Full PR body at https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13126. Root cause: YOLO toggle was cosmetic, approval path never read it. Fix: remove setting, make auto-approve menu single source of truth, add v3 storage migration.
- **Category**: core. **Size**: ~3h. **Priority**: SKIP (no YOLO mode).

#### 2. MCP hung-server 3s initialize cap (mcp, ~2h, LOW)

- **What**: Cline #13086 cap default MCP initialize budget at 3s to protect session creation. MCP initialize runs on the session.create critical path, which the hub caps at 30s, and connect() can spend the budget twice (newline then Content-Length framing). The 30s default from #13067 meant a server that never initializes held session.create for up to 60s, so the hub RPC timed out and the CLI tore the whole session down and exited. Return to the pre-#13067 shape with a bigger probe: 3s instead of 1.5s. That still covers the ~2s starters the old probe killed (#13035) and keeps the worst case at ~6s per server, far under the hub deadline. Genuinely slow starters (JVM-based servers like Oracle SQLcl) now need an explicit timeout in cline_mcp_settings.json, which continues to override the default in either direction. Tests: update slow-start regression tests to new policy (2s connects by default, 4s connects with configured timeout), refresh displayed initialize-timeout assertions, add invariant test keeping doubled default well under HUB_DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS.
- **Why**: Alexi has MCP support (src/mcp/client.ts). src/mcp/client.ts:180 has `DEFAULT_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 30000` (same 30s value as pre-fix Cline). Same issue exists: a hung MCP server could block session creation for up to 60s (doubled newline+framed), exceeding any reasonable CLI deadline. Would be LOW priority (robustness fix, prevents hung MCP servers from killing session creation). Size ~2h: change DEFAULT_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS from 30000 to 3000 in src/mcp/client.ts:180, verify config override works (src/mcp/config.ts has timeout.startup field already, src/mcp/client.ts:1339 resolves startup timeout with fallback precedence), add tests (hung server skipped instead of blocking session creation, configured timeout overrides default, multiple slow servers stay under deadline), update docs (document 3s default, note JVM-based servers need explicit timeout in mcp-servers.json). Category: mcp. Priority: LOW (robustness fix, prevents hung servers from killing sessions, protects critical path).
- **Source**: Cline PR #13086 "fix(mcp): cap the default initialize budget at 3s to protect session creation" (merged 2026-08-10, commit sha unknown). Full PR body at https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13086. Supersedes startup-budget approach with simple constant fix. 30s default meant hung server held session.create for up to 60s, hub RPC timed out, CLI exited. 3s instead of 1.5s probe covers ~2s starters, worst case ~6s per server.
- **Category**: mcp. **Size**: ~2h. **Priority**: LOW.

#### 3. Claude 4.5/4.6/4.7 model support (providers, ~2h, MODERATE)

- **What**: Aider #5173 expand ANTHROPIC_MODELS list with recent Claude model names. `ANTHROPIC_MODELS` in `aider/models.py` is used by `sanity_check_models` to map a bare Claude model name (no provider prefix) to the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable. Models not in this list fall through to the keymap provider lookup. The list was stale — it had claude-2, 3.x family, claude-3-5-*, claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-opus-4-20250514, plus 4.5/4.6/4.7 unrounded names — but was missing: claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219, claude-opus-4-1 / claude-opus-4-1-20250805, claude-opus-4-5 / claude-opus-4-5-20251101, claude-opus-4-6-20260205 (dated variant), claude-opus-4-7-20260416 (dated variant). All added names have corresponding entries in `aider/resources/model-settings.yml`. Also added bash tree-sitter tags for repomap support (#5132), gpt-5.5 model settings across providers, updated model alias expectations for sonnet and opus, added Claude Opus 4.7 model settings for Bedrock/Vertex/OpenRouter, disabled temperature for opus-4 models, gated thinking_tokens, mapped opus and sonnet aliases to latest Claude models, added Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.7 model support, enabled overeager mode for Claude Sonnet 4.5 models.
- **Why**: Alexi uses SAP AI Core orchestration proxy (src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts), model IDs prefixed `sap-ai-core/anthropic--*`. Would be MODERATE priority (keep provider layer current, enables new Claude models as SAP AI Core deploys them). Size ~2h: check if Alexi model registry needs updates (src/providers/index.ts getProviderForModel dispatches by model id prefix `sap-ai-core/anthropic--*`; verify new opus/sonnet IDs route correctly), add any missing Claude 4.5/4.6/4.7 models to routing-config.json (if used; check routing-config.example.json for model examples), verify SAP AI Core orchestration proxy supports new models (check AICORE_MODEL env var examples in .env.example, verify SAP deployment availability), add tests (new model IDs route to correct provider, temperature handling for opus-4 models per Aider fix - disable deprecated temperature for Claude 4 models, src/providers/transform.ts handles temperature). Category: providers. Priority: MODERATE (keep provider layer current, enables new models).
- **Source**: Aider PR #5173 "Expand ANTHROPIC_MODELS list with recent Claude model names" (merged 2026-08-10, commit sha unknown). Full PR body at https://github.com/aider-ai/aider/pull/5173. Companion to OPENAI_MODELS list expansion. Aider also shipped bash tree-sitter tags (#5132), gpt-5.5 model settings, alias updates, Opus 4.7 Bedrock/Vertex/OpenRouter, temperature disable for opus-4, thinking_tokens gating, sonnet/opus alias mapping, Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.7 support, overeager mode for Sonnet 4.5.
- **Category**: providers. **Size**: ~2h. **Priority**: MODERATE.
